Adapa – Standard Babylonian -: “The Choicest Of [Unders]tanding … […]”

  • Translation: Benjamin R. Foster

Per line: N = normalized Akkadian reconstruction (| metrical foot, || caesura); T = eBL English translation; L = lemmas with eBL dictionary glosses; then notes, parallel lines, and the manuscripts' transliterations (ATF). a+1

  • N: [tašī]mtu nisiqša? ... [ ... ]
  • T: The choicest of [unders]tanding … […]
  • L: [tašī]mtu ← tašīmtu I “discernment, sagacity of deities, humans”; nisiqša? ← nisqu I “choice, selection”
  • Note: Alternatively, restore šīmtu “destiny”.
UncNA1 o i 1'. [ta-ši]m-tu₄ ni-siq?#-ša₂?# x [x x x x x x x x (x)]

a+2

  • N: [q]ibīssu kīma qibīt āni lū magr[at?]
  • T: His command was compli[ed with], like the command of Anu.
  • L: [q]ibīssu ← qibītu I “speech”; kīma ← kīma I “like”; qibīt ← qibītu I “speech”; āni ← Anu I “An(um) (the god of heaven) OAkk, Bab.”; lū ← lū I “let it be”; magr[at?] ← magāru I “to consent, agree”
  • Note: The sign AN might also be read DINGIR, i.e. qibīt ili “the command of a god” (but see also l. e+6).
UncNA1 o i 2'. [q]i₂-bit-su ki-ma qi₂-bit# DINGIR lu#-u₂# ma#-ag*#-r[at?]

a+3

  • T: He made him perfect in [wi]sdom, revealing (to him) the designs of the land.
  • L: [u]zna ← uznu I “f. ear”; rapašta ← rapšu I “f. rapaš/ltu(m) wide, extended of building, object, road”; ušaklilšu ← šuklulu II; uṣurāt ← uṣurtu I “drawing, plan Bab., NA”; māti ← mātu I “f. land, country”; kullumu ← kullumu I
UncNA1 o i 3'. [u]z-na DAGAL-tu₄ u₂-šak-lil-šu₂ u₂-ṣu-rat KUR kul!(MU)-lu-mu#

a+4

  • N: ana šuātu nēmeqa iddiššu napišta dārīta ul iddiššu
  • T: To him he granted wisdom, eternal life he did not grant him.
  • L: ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; šuātu ← šuāti I “m. & f.”; nēmeqa ← nēmequ I “wisdom, sagacity Bab., M/NA civilising knowledge”; iddiššu ← nadānu II “to give”; napišta ← napištu I “throat, life OAkk ?, Bab. (Ass. cf. napaštum”; dārīta ← dārû I “lasting, eternal Bab., NA of gods, royal offspring”; ul ← ul I “not Bab., to negate main clause”; iddiššu ← nadānu II “to give”
  • Parallels: cf. (Adapa Sum. Meturan 65a)

  • T: In those days, in those years, this sage, the citizen of Eridu,

a+6

  • N: ea kīma šeddi ina amīlūti ibnīšu
  • T: Ea made him like a protective spirit among men.
  • L: ea ← Ea I; kīma ← kīma I “like”; šeddi ← šēdu I “protective deity”; ina ← ina I “(im-m..., ip-p... etc.) in, on”; amīlūti ← awīlūtu I “humanity”; ibnīšu ← banû IV “to create”

a+17

  • N: šarru? ea ina mayyāli ina šadādi
  • T: While king Ea was stretched out in bed,
  • L: šarru? ← šarru I “pl. šarrū, šarrānu king”; ea ← Ea I; ina ← ina I “(im-m..., ip-p... etc.) in, on”; mayyāli ← mayyālu I “bed, resting place Bab., M/NA euph. for grave”; ina ← ina I “(im-m..., ip-p... etc.) in, on”; šadādi ← šadādu I “to drag”
  • Note: Judging from the photograph of the tablet in [RN493: 174=Pl. 1], there does not seem to be room for another sign to the left of RU at the beginning of the line. For the various suggestions made for this line, which all but one involve restoring such an extra sign, see [RN303: 129], as well as [RN493: 9; 13f.], who is the only one to read the line with RU only, namely as nadi “(he was) lying”. For the latter see, however, [RN1364: 395], who points out that such logographic writings are quite uncommon in literary compositions. For the emendation to šarru “king” employed here, see l. c+8 ana šarri ea. In essence, it goes back to a suggestion by M. Gallery apud [RN162: 345 fn. 5].
UncNA1 o i 17'. <šar>-ru {d}e₂-a ina ma-a-a-li ina ša₂-da-di
